We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(x),$ ${v}_{2}(x),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dy\,dx={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,{y}^{3}\le z\le 2}
$$

Now, let's sketch the region. Since it is a type I region, we first sketch the projection onto the $xy$-plane, given by

$$
E={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{2}}.
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/58a9056015b3dad91ec7ae64bff893c8c6c2cce6480c979545e423cbe105ef03.png)

Then, the region $R$ is shown in the diagram below, where ${y}^{3}\le z\le 2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/2fdd6a15b4ddadfc3ee24af5e35e2a87e9e963ceeefbf858b704d78ee0b78513.png)

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/65da730d32f200b8f9da004ee8cf6b7e79095e323961f4a5b6dfa0bddeace42b.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=(x,z),$ is

$$
z={y}^{3}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt[3]{z}
$$

- The left boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/1743f540a85fc1c266c84da8f34b2012516b7bbc98d113cf7c62ba3bba8173c1.png)

We now consider the projection $D$ as a type II plane region in the $xz$-plane with the top curve given by 

$$
z=(\sqrt[3]{2})^{3}=2.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/b76bf84e1179bec6a1e8e357c6cc628eee95c1663e6f0ff375135612a6f275de.png)

Hence,

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,0\le z\le 2}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dy\,dx={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{z}}f(x,y,z)\,\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$
